added.title: Director of Inference Infrastructure Engineering
added.description:
About the Company

Edge Inference Inc. is building the nationwide AI inference network — a distributed fabric of Inference Points that puts GPU compute within single-digit milliseconds of where inference is actually consumed. Training happens in a handful of giant campuses; inference happens everywhere, continuously, and it is latency-bound, sovereignty-bound, and cost-bound in ways training is not. Anchored by 348 Prime Group Holdings-owned sites across 28 U.S. states and 3 Canadian provinces, we convert an existing national land position into the densest inference footprint in North America — 200 Inference Points energized within 36 months. That target is only reachable if every IP is cut from the same frozen design.

About the Role

The Director of Inference Infrastructure Engineering owns the IP Standard Design (IPSD) — the frozen, repeatable reference build from which every Inference Point is manufactured. This is a product management role disguised as an engineering leadership role: the IPSD is Edge Inference's most valuable intellectual property, and the difference between a 200-site rollout and a 20-site rollout is whether that design stays frozen, stays buildable, and gets cheaper per MW with every Deployment Wave. You lead the internal engineering team and the external MEP consultant bench, run engineering release management across Deployment Waves, own value engineering of the cost per MW energized, and close the feedback loop from commissioning and NIOC operations back into the next IPSD revision. You also own the Spoke, Satellite, and Hub design derivatives that sit above the IP tier.

Responsibilities

Own the IP Standard Design end to end — electrical one-lines, mechanical flow diagrams, structural and civil packages, rack elevations, and the controls/telemetry stack — as a frozen, versioned product rather than a per-site custom design.
Run engineering release management across Deployment Waves: publish a numbered IPSD revision per wave, freeze it before long-lead procurement, and enforce a formal change-control board for any deviation requested by a site, a customer, or an AHJ.
Value engineer the cost per MW energized wave over wave — targeting a documented reduction in $/MW and $/rack across the first three waves through prefabrication, standardized BOMs, vendor consolidation, and design simplification.
Lead and grow the internal engineering team (electrical, mechanical, controls, structural) and manage the external MEP consultant bench, including scope definition, fee negotiation, deliverable quality, and stamped-drawing accountability across many states.
Engineer the IP power and thermal envelope for 30–130 kW/rack GPU density: 2N power topology, medium-voltage switchgear, N+1 direct-to-chip liquid cooling with CDUs, rear-door heat exchangers, facility water loops, and dry coolers sized for a national range of climates.
Own the BESS design standard (LFP chemistry) per NFPA 855, including behind-the-meter generation options, ISO/RTO market participation capability, and grid interconnect strategy where utility capacity is the binding constraint.
Define the design derivatives above the IP tier — Spoke (3–6 MW), Satellite (7–10 MW), and Hub (10–20 MW) — so that regional aggregation, model caching, and IX peering requirements are engineered rather than improvised.
Close the design feedback loop: institutionalize a commissioning-to-design and NIOC-to-design channel so every Level 4/5 commissioning finding, energization defect, and operational failure mode is triaged into the IPSD backlog with an owner and a target release.
Validate the design against the GPU platform roadmap — NVIDIA GB200/GB300 NVL72, HGX H200, L40S, RTX PRO Blackwell Server Edition, AMD Instinct MI300X/MI355X — so an IP energized in wave one can accept the silicon of wave four without a structural rebuild.
Partner with the Deployment Project Management team on constructability, prefab/skid packaging, factory acceptance testing, and the sequencing that lets many small parallel sites energize on a predictable cadence.
Own design compliance across jurisdictions: Uptime Institute Tier III/IV alignment where a Hub requires it, NFPA 70E, NFPA 855, local energy codes, and PE-stamped submittal packages in every state in the rollout.
Serve as the engineering authority in customer technical diligence for large Inference Capacity Agreements, defending the design to Priority Class I–II customers and their consultants.

Qualifications

10+ years of data center or critical infrastructure engineering experience, with 4+ years leading an engineering team or an owner-side design function.
Demonstrated ownership of a standardized, repeatable build — a reference design, prototype, or product-ized facility rolled out across multiple sites, not a portfolio of one-off custom projects.
Deep high-density design experience: liquid cooling (DLC, CDUs, rear-door heat exchangers), 2N electrical topology, medium-voltage distribution, and rack densities above 40 kW.
Experience managing external MEP consultants and prefabrication or skid vendors, including BOM control, factory acceptance testing, and multi-state permitting support.
PE license (Electrical or Mechanical) or the demonstrated ability to lead a stamped design program through licensed engineers of record.
Fluency in the operational metrics the design is judged by: PUE, WUE, $/MW energized, GPU fleet availability, and Inference Point uptime targets of 99.99%.
Bachelor's degree in Electrical or Mechanical Engineering or a related discipline.

Required Skills

Data center or critical infrastructure engineering leadership.
Standardized, repeatable build and reference design ownership.
High-density design including liquid cooling, 2N electrical topology, and medium-voltage distribution.
Management of external MEP consultants and prefabrication or skid vendors.
Ability to lead stamped design programs through licensed engineers of record.
Understanding of operational metrics such as PUE, WUE, $/MW energized, GPU fleet availability, and high uptime targets.

Preferred Skills

Direct experience designing for NVIDIA GB200/GB300 NVL72 or comparable rack-scale GPU systems, including NVL-class power shelves and liquid-cooled rack integration.
BESS design experience under NFPA 855, including LFP systems, ISO/RTO market participation, or behind-the-meter generation.
Uptime Institute ATD or Tier Certification of Design
Modular, prefabricated, or edge data center product development background.
Familiarity with GPU east-west fabric requirements — InfiniBand NDR/XDR, Spectrum-X, 400G/800G optics — and their structured cabling and pathway implications.
Experience supporting a rollout across 20+ jurisdictions with varying utility, code, and interconnect regimes.

Highly competitive compensation inclusive of base salary, long term incentives, robust benefit package including employer sponsored 401(k) match.

Upstate Coin & Gold is seeking a deeply technical, commercially minded technology leader
to help shape the next chapter of our growth. As we expand, diversify, and invest in technology, this leader will build the systems, capabilities, and team that help us stay ahead. The opportunity: scale the technology behind a growing precious metals business, accelerate new products and services, and turn our ambition for industry technology leadership into a widening competitive advantage.

This opportunity is particularly well suited for an accomplished Senior Director ready to step into a Vice President role
, or a VP who remains close to the technology and the work. Prior VP experience is not required. We value technical credibility, commercial judgment, execution discipline, and exceptional communication and collaboration. You should be equally effective leading engineers, partnering with executives, and working with stakeholders throughout the company.

The role

Reporting directly to the CEO, you will lead a multidisciplinary technology team of approximately 15–20 employees
and own our complete technology environment: PlatformGold®
, software development, product execution, data, AI and automation, AWS, NetSuite, Salesforce, enterprise applications, integrations, cybersecurity, and all company IT, systems, networks, hardware, and end-user technology.

The CEO sets strategic, product, and innovation direction. You provide candid technical advice and turn that direction into reliable, scalable solutions and measurable business results. Your scope will expand as the company grows and diversifies.

This is an in-office position, not remote or hybrid
, based primarily at our Centennial headquarters. Expect approximately six business days each month in Boulder
, plus periodic travel to our Fayetteville, New York office, other company and partner locations, and relevant conferences.

What you’ll deliver

Technical leadership with real depth. Stay close to architecture, code, cloud infrastructure, APIs, and data. Work alongside engineers on complex decisions and problems without becoming the primary developer or a bottleneck.
Business value and delivery velocity. Focus resources on transformative, well-supported opportunities. Understand full project costs, budgets, capacity, opportunity cost, and cost of delay; simplify, defer, or stop lower-value work and defend priorities constructively with stakeholders.
Accountable execution. Set credible scope, budgets, milestones, and delivery commitments. Deliver on time or early and at or below approved budgets, surfacing risks early and measuring outcomes after launch. Value engineer faster, simpler, more economical solutions without compromising essential quality or controls.
A stronger technology team. Recruit, coach, and develop strong talent and future leaders. Set clear ownership, address performance, build succession and backup coverage, and keep the team’s skills and practices current as technology changes.
Dependable customer and employee technology. Advance PlatformGold® and its APIs, where usability, speed, pricing and data accuracy, and reliability matter. Own enterprise systems, integrations, cybersecurity, IT support, hardware, continuity, and recovery across the company.
A growing technology advantage. Evaluate and adopt useful advances in AI, automation, and engineering practices. Build reusable capabilities for new business lines, assess technology implications of partnerships or acquisitions under consideration, and track delivery, reliability, customer outcomes, and technology economics.

Qualifications

Typically 12+ years of progressive technical experience and 5+ years of increasing leadership responsibility, including substantial firsthand engineering or architecture experience and recent technical involvement.
Readiness to lead a 15–20-person multidisciplinary technology team, supported by experience developing technical leaders and delivering business-critical systems.
Strong working knowledge of modern software engineering, AWS, APIs, databases, CI/CD, testing, observability, security, enterprise applications, and IT. Experience with NetSuite and Salesforce, or comparable ERP and CRM platforms, is valuable.
Practical familiarity with AI-assisted development, LLMs, and automation, plus a demonstrated habit of learning and helping teams adopt better tools and methods.
Evidence of commercial judgment, value engineering, disciplined budgeting, and delivery—not just technical expertise.
Excellent communication and collaboration: clear explanations, attentive listening, constructive disagreement, and the ability to build trust and alignment at every level. Low ego, high standards, and strong follow-through.
A relevant degree or equivalent professional experience. Leadership capability and results matter more than title history.

$220,000–$255,000 base salary
, based on experience and qualifications, plus an annual performance bonus opportunity. Benefits include up to a 6% 401(k) company match

Overview

North America Supply Chain is moving from a traditional enterprise technology model to an empowered product operating model. Product Management, Design, and Data capabilities are being established; now we need an engineering leader to build the product engineering capability that brings the model to life at scale.

This is a hands-on build-and-transform leadership mandate, not a traditional systems-administration role focused on building the engineering organization behind North America Supply Chain. Reporting to the Head of Engineering & Platform for North America, you will build and lead the supply chain engineering team responsible for the products that power planning, sourcing, manufacturing, warehousing, logistics, and fulfillment.

Our supply chain spans company-owned plants, co-manufacturing partners, suppliers, and distribution networks, creating significant operational complexity. Your mandate is to build high-performing, product-minded engineering teams that modernize critical systems, improve visibility and decision-making, and deliver measurable business outcomes.

What you will own

Supply chain engineering build-out. Build the engineering team, operating rhythms, technical standards, and management practices needed to support a modern product operating model within supply chain. Hire, coach, and develop engineering managers, senior engineers, architects, and product-minded teams capable of owning complex supply chain products and platforms end to end. 
Organization stewardship. Own engineering capacity, talent strategy, partner/vendor decisions, and engineering investment trade-offs. Partner with Product and business leaders to align engineering capacity to the highest-value Supply Chain outcomes while increasing internal capability and improving delivery economics.
Domain-specific technical leadership. Partner with supply chain product, design, data, operations, and business leaders to translate operational priorities into durable technical capabilities. Focus engineering energy on the systems and workflows that matter most across planning, manufacturing, logistics, quality, warehousing, fulfillment, and customer service workflows. 
Product-engineering partnership. Operate as the senior engineering counterpart to supply chain product leadership. Ensure engineers participate early in discovery, shape feasibility and sequencing, and stay accountable for outcomes rather than handoffs or outputs. 
Engineering excellence. Establish standards and metrics for reliability, deployment frequency, cycle time, quality, security, observability, incident learning, and measurable business impact. Make technical debt visible as an operational and business trade-off, not just an engineering concern. 
AI, automation, and engineering productivity. Use AI, automation, integration patterns, and platform engineering to improve developer productivity, supply chain decision quality, workflow automation, and service experiences. Establish responsible guardrails for data readiness, controls, security, compliance, and human-in-the-loop decisioning. 
Portfolio and enterprise leadership. Translate architecture, reliability, delivery, and investment choices into clear business risk and opportunity. Partner with the Head of Engineering and NAOU leaders to align roadmap, funding, headcount, vendor strategy, and platform priorities. 
Capability Transition. Build a deliberate mix of internal and partner engineering capability, using external talent to accelerate delivery while systematically increasing critical engineering knowledge and ownership within TCCC.

Qualifications

Required

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Supply Chain, or a related technical field 
12+ years of software, platform, or enterprise engineering experience, including 5+ years leading managers or multi-team engineering organizations
Proven track record building and scaling engineering teams, including defining the hiring bar, team topology, technical standards, operating rhythms, and leadership expectations. 
Experience delivering engineering solutions for supply chain, manufacturing, logistics, fulfillment, operations, or similar 
Strong technical background in modern enterprise architecture, including distributed systems, API and integration platforms, data pipelines or data products, cloud-native architectures, observability, and secure software delivery. 
Experience modernizing legacy, vendor-heavy, or highly integrated systems while maintaining business continuity, using pragmatic build, buy, and partner decisions. 
Demonstrated ability to partner with Product Management, Design, Data, Operations, and business leaders to move from project-based delivery to outcome-oriented product engineering. 
Experience leading multi-domain engineering portfolios with competing priorities, complex dependencies, and senior stakeholder needs. 
Strong understanding of supply chain performance drivers, including service levels, OTIF, inventory, capacity, throughput, quality, logistics, and operational resilience. 
Proven ability to develop engineering leaders, align cross-functional stakeholders, and navigate complex organizational dynamics with clarity, accountability, and inclusion. 

Preferred

Advanced degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Supply Chain, Operations, Analytics, or Business Administration. 
Experience in CPG, manufacturing, retail, logistics, industrial technology, or other large-scale operational environments. 
Experience working within ERP-enabled supply chain environments, including SAP S/4HANA or equivalent enterprise platforms. 
Familiarity with manufacturing execution systems, warehouse management systems, transportation management systems, or supply chain planning tools such as Blue Yonder, o9, Kinaxis, or similar. 
Experience with real-time data streaming, IoT or manufacturing data, data platforms, analytics, AI, or automation used to improve operational decision-making. 
Experience leading digital or product-model transformation within a large, matrixed, multi-geography enterprise. 

Leadership Attributes

Builder Leadership Creates and scales high-performing engineering organizations through strong talent, clear standards, and a culture of accountability.
Technical Judgment Makes sound architectural, platform, and investment decisions that balance speed, quality, risk, and long-term sustainability.
Enterprise Influence Builds alignment across Product, Data, Operations, and Business leaders to drive shared outcomes and priorities.
Transformational Leadership Leads through ambiguity and change, modernizing legacy environments while maintaining business continuity.
Operational Impact Connects technology investments to measurable supply chain outcomes including service, productivity, quality, and resilience.
Product Mindset

Brings engineering into discovery early, challenges assumptions with technical insight, and builds teams accountable for improving outcomes over time rather than simply delivering requirements.
